question: with only the 20 describe sentences in training, can the read-out recover object and place on the 60 paraphrase sentences whose entity names never occur in training?

definition.train: the 20 describe sentences, one per (object, place) goal; no paraphrase.
definition.test: the 60 needs / hope / state sentences (3 per goal).  No test sentence has a training counterpart and the split is by variant, not by fold.
definition.leak_check: for every object and place name, assert the name string does not occur in any of the 20 training sentences; the count of test sentences that do contain their own name is reported so the mapping is verifiable rather than assumed.
definition.readout: closed form ridge W = (X^T X + lambda I)^-1 X^T Y; prediction is the arg-max over the held-out rows.  One matrix solve per (arm, lambda, fold, target); no gradient step.
definition.joint: fraction of the 60 held-out rows where object AND place are both correct.

criteria.per_arm: readable iff joint >= 0.75 and object >= 0.85 and place >= 0.80; not_readable iff joint <= chance + 0.10; otherwise inconclusive.  A degenerate read-out (one predicted class for object or for place) is inconclusive, never not_readable.
criteria.overall: cross_family_semantic_bridge if any arm is readable; cross_family_zero_shot_fails if every available arm is not_readable; otherwise inconclusive.
criteria.lambda: the reported reading is the best joint accuracy over the four lambdas.
criteria.no_fit: 0 training, 0 optimizer steps, 0 Adam, 0 confirm, 0 new parameters.
criteria.frozen: thresholds and both splits are fixed before the first reading.
